neighbours.label: ' to' that introduces the purpose or intended result of an action someone performs on another person or thing ('shaking an infant to make him stop', 'for the monkey to take')
fire: Neglect may be one event, such as a nurse slapping a patient to make her stop shouting; it may also last for years.
Cruelty can be a single act, such as an owner kicking a dog to make it stop barking; it can also be constant.
Bullying may be a lone incident, such as a pupil shoving a classmate to make him hand over money; it may also be daily.
Harm can come from one moment, such as a coach grabbing a player to make her sit down; it can also build slowly.
Abuse might be a brief episode, such as a guard striking a prisoner to make him keep quiet; it might also be routine.
Mistreatment may be a single case, such as a babysitter pinching a toddler to make him stop whining; it may also recur.
Violence can be one outburst, such as a driver hitting a horse to make it move faster; it can also be habitual.
Assault may be a single event, such as a brother pushing his sister to make her leave the room; it may also be repeated.
quiet: Neglect may be one event, such as a nurse forgetting a patient during a busy shift; it may also last for years.
Cruelty can be a single act, such as an owner leaving a dog outside in the snow; it can also be constant.
Bullying may be a lone incident, such as a pupil mocking a classmate in the hallway; it may also be daily.
Harm can come from one moment, such as a coach shouting at a player during practice; it can also build slowly.
Abuse might be a brief episode, and most guards say they want to go home without any trouble; it might also be routine.
Mistreatment may be a single case, and the babysitter walked to the park with the toddler afterwards; it may also recur.
Violence can be one outburst, such as a driver and a horse startled by thunder; it can also be habitual.
Assault may be a single event, and the brother later apologised to his sister in the kitchen; it may also be repeated.

notes: Card: ' to' x11 of the top 32, after an object noun and before the intended result (shaking an infant to make..., for the monkey to take..., transfer your balances to...). Weak pole (max 8.5). Probes: 'a parent hitting a child to make him stop talking' .67, 'move your debt to a lender' .26, 'for blood to reach' .17; short purpose sentences ('used a hammer to break') .02, 'want to go' .05. Low confidence: only long, card-like sentences fired.
